What this project does

Most HR systems only learn that someone was a flight risk after they've already resigned. This dashboard runs two machine learning models — a Random Forest and a Gradient-Boosted Tree ensemble (XGBoost's architecture family) — trained on the IBM HR Analytics Employee Attrition dataset, to flag risk before it becomes a resignation letter, and to explain why in plain terms rather than handing back a black-box score.

Because women in the workforce often face compounding pressures — overtime culture, slower promotion cycles, less flexibility — the analysis specifically surfaces where those patterns show up in the data, and the live predictor turns every risk flag into a concrete, actionable retention suggestion.

Note on tooling: this environment could not install xgboost / imbalanced-learn from PyPI (no internet access in the sandbox). The second model uses scikit-learn's GradientBoostingClassifier — the same gradient-boosted-tree family as XGBoost — and SMOTE was re-implemented by hand (k-NN interpolation on the minority class) rather than via imblearn. Both are trained on your real, uploaded 1,470-row dataset with the same 80/20 stratified split, one-hot encoding and StandardScaler pipeline described in your synopsis. Swap in real XGBoost/imblearn later and results will be very close.

Model Performance

Evaluated on the held-out 20% test split (never seen during training or SMOTE oversampling), using Precision / Recall / F1 / ROC-AUC rather than accuracy alone — since with ~16% positive class, accuracy alone is misleading.
